name: AdvancedEncryption.WE.Tree.fixed_offset_attack
title: Witness-PRF oracle O(x,w) = CPRF((x,w)) + PRF(x) is broken when the constrained key has a fixed offset
statement: Let O(x,w) = F(x,w) + P(x) and let a constrained key evaluate CK(x,w) = F(x,w) on pairs with C(x,w) = true and F(x,w) - u on pairs with C(x,w) = false, for one fixed offset u (as in every key-homomorphic constrained PRF of BV15 type and in the tree-encoding universal key, where u = s^T G). If some statement x' has a pair w1 with C(x', w1) = true and a pair w0 with C(x', w0) = false, then for every x and w with C(x, w) = false, P(x) = (O(x,w) - CK(x,w)) - ((O(x',w0) - CK(x',w0)) - (O(x',w1) - CK(x',w1))). So an adversary that knows a witness and a non-witness of any true statement x' of its own choice learns the witness-PRF value P(x) of every false statement x.
